# Teaching the Machine {.unnumbered}

\lettrine{I}{n} conventional machine learning, data is passive and computational cost is paid in cloud kilowatt-hours. Datasets are scraped from the internet, curated, partitioned into training and validation splits, and treated as an exogenous ground truth ($x \sim P_{\text{data}}$). A vision classifier or language model inspects this data from behind glass; its predictions have no physical momentum and no causal power to alter the distribution of the documents it will encounter tomorrow. If a classifier mispredicts a label, the error is isolated—the physical world remains completely unaffected.

In Physical AI, this assumption collapses entirely. The data distribution of a physical machine is **endogenous**: the machine participates in a closed causal loop where every motor command changes the configuration of the physical plant, directly dictating what its sensors will observe next ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$). Because the policy creates its own future sensory inputs, training an embodied model is not an exercise in curve-fitting; it is the deliberate management of **latent failure debts**.

::: {#pri-vol4-endogenous-drift .callout-principle title="The endogenous feedback law"}

**Invariant**: Unlike static vision or language models ($x \sim P_{\text{data}}$), embodied actions alter future sensory states ($s_{t+1} \sim P(s \mid s_t, a_t)$). Under pure open-loop behavioral cloning with single-step error rate $\epsilon$, trajectory drift compounds quadratically over horizon $T$:
$$ \mathbb{E}[\text{Error}_T] = \mathcal{O}(T^2 \epsilon) $$

**Implication**: Open-loop imitation on expert-only demonstrations is structurally unstable. Training pipelines must inject corrective feedback—either via closed-loop human interventions (DAgger), noise-injection perturbation rollouts, or reinforcement learning with real or simulated physics.

:::

Part II guides students through the three stages of teaching an embodied machine:

* **Data as Physical Experience (@sec-data):** Every demonstration collected in the physical world consumes mechanical life—wearing cycloidal gearboxes, draining battery energy, heating motor stators, and accumulating sensor calibration drift. We examine the systems physics of bilateral teleoperation, multi-camera SerDes timestamp synchronization, and the Four-Stream Action Tap Tuple. We show why logging human recovery interventions is mathematically required to prevent compounding covariate drift ($O(T^2 \epsilon)$) and keep the machine on its demonstration manifold.
* **Policy Training and Latent Debts (@sec-training):** Formulating policy architectures that can generate high-dimensional continuous trajectories without suffering mode collapse. We analyze the fundamental policy synthesis trade-offs across Behavioral Cloning, Offline RL, and Sim-to-Real RL. We explain why naive Mean Squared Error (MSE) fails on multimodal human actions (averaging two valid paths into an obstacle) and why Action Chunking with Transformers (ACT) and Diffusion Policies succeed by predicting continuous trajectory splines. Crucially, we decompose the sim-to-real reality gap into friction hysteresis, structural compliance, and motor phase lag.
* **Evaluation as Closed-Loop Reality (@sec-evaluation):** Confronting why offline test-set accuracy is fundamentally decoupled from physical survival. A policy achieving $99\%$ open-loop accuracy on a static validation set can fail within seconds when closed in a real feedback loop due to non-Lipschitz sensitivity and compounding error. We establish the systems discipline of closed-loop evaluation—applying non-asymptotic Clopper-Pearson coverage bounds, Butler & Finelli exposure limits, and Extreme Value Theory to evaluate tail-risk safety.

::: {#pri-vol4-action-chunking .callout-principle title="Multimodal trajectory integrity"}

**Invariant**: Demonstrations in continuous physical space are inherently multimodal. Regressing a unimodal loss (such as Mean Squared Error) across divergent demonstration paths averages physically viable trajectories into an unviable mean state (e.g., driving straight into an obstacle that demonstrators avoided to the left or right).

**Implication**: Physical AI policies must predict continuous probability distributions over actions (Diffusion Policies) or synthesize continuous temporal splines over an $H$-step horizon (Action Chunking with Transformers, ACT). Predicting action chunks preserves high-frequency kinematic correlations and dampens single-step execution jitter.

:::

::: {#pri-vol4-closed-loop-reality .callout-principle title="The benchmark decoupling law"}

**Invariant**: Open-loop validation error exhibits near-zero correlation with closed-loop physical survival rate ($R_{\text{closed}}$). Because physical dynamics are non-Lipschitz at contact boundaries and obstacle interfaces, an open-loop validation accuracy of $99.9\%$ can still result in a $100\%$ collision rate.

**Implication**: Evaluation pipelines must prioritize closed-loop physical rollouts under adversarial perturbation over static test-set accuracy. Statistical safety claims require Clopper-Pearson binomial coverage bounds and extreme value tail analysis rather than average-case validation metrics.

:::

Part II teaches students how to curate physical data, train generative action policies, and measure closed-loop survival without falling into the trap of superficial benchmark optimism.
